In contrast to older children and adults, newborns with clavicle fractures often do not require immobilization. Instead, they are usually treated with simple observation and parental education on how to handle the baby to avoid exacerbating the injury. In older children and adults, however, clavicle fractures may require immobilization with a figure-of-eight sling or arm sling, followed by rehabilitation exercises to restore range of motion and strength to the shoulder and arm. Overall, the management of clavicle fractures in newborns is more conservative and focused on supportive care, whereas in older children and adults, it may involve more active treatment and rehabilitation to ensure proper healing and prevent long-term complications.
